title: CFGL-LCR: A Counterfactual Graph Learning Framework for Legal Case Retrieval

problem.claim: Legal case retrieval seeks relevant cases from short case descriptions and is important to modern legal systems.

gap.claim: Existing methods underrepresent semantic associations among legal elements and face insufficient training data because relevant-case labels are difficult to annotate.

contributions.claim: The framework transforms legal case documents into graphs and models legal-element semantics with a graph neural network.
A counterfactual data generator augments counterfactual data to address low-resource learning and improve legal case representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on two publicly available legal benchmarks show CFGL-LCR significantly outperforming previous state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Legal case retrieval supports finding relevant cases from short descriptions.
Existing methods inadequately model legal-element semantics and suffer from limited training data.
The paper proposes a counterfactual graph learning framework.
The framework uses graph neural networks for legal-element semantics and counterfactual generation for data augmentation and representation learning.
Experiments on two public benchmarks are reported to outperform prior state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two legal benchmarks.
The abstract does not provide metrics, numerical results, baselines, or implementation details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, causal validity, or reproducibility.
